title: Employ staff under the Registered and Licensed Clubs Award 2020
what: Pay and employ staff at no less than the terms of the Registered and Licensed Clubs Award 2020.

sources.title: Registered and Licensed Clubs Award 2020
sources.quote: 4.1 This industry award covers employers of employees engaged in the performance of all or any work in or in connection with or for clubs and their employees in the classifications within Schedule A —Classification Definitions , to the exclusion of any other modern award.

reach.note: National system employers that are companies, in every state.

sources.title: Registered and Licensed Clubs Award 2020
sources.quote: 4.3 Club means any club which is registered and licensed under the provisions of relevant State or Commonwealth Statutes ( Liquor and/or Gaming Acts, Associations’ Incorporation Acts or Corporations Acts ) and which is established and operates on a not-for-profit basis for the benefit of members and the community.

sources.title: Which system of employment laws applies
sources.publisher: Government of Western Australia (Private Sector Labour Relations)
sources.quote: The state system covers: Private sector businesses and their employees that operate as: Sole traders. Partnerships, where none of the partners in the business is a constitutional corporation (trading or financial corporation).

confidence_note: Registered or licensed clubs (cl 4.3), matched to the ABS class for hospitality clubs.

assessment.summary: The Registered and Licensed Clubs Award sets the industry's classifications, minimum pay, allowances and penalty rates on top of the National Employment Standards.

marks.reason: Classifications, allowances, penalty rates and their record-keeping add to the cost and complexity of employing in the industry.
